previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted following a mechanical fall that resulted in a left intertrochanteric femur fracture. She underwent successful open reduction and internal fixation with a cephalomedullary nail. Her hospital course was complicated by opioid-induced nausea and a gastroparesis flare, which resolved with methylnaltrexone. A urinary tract infection was treated with antibiotics, and urinary retention improved with intermittent catheterization. Her end-stage renal disease was managed with continued peritoneal dialysis, and metabolic acidosis was corrected with oral bicarbonate. Phosphate control was addressed with lanthanum due to intolerance of sevelamer. Chronic pain and fibromyalgia were managed with uptitrated nortriptyline and pregabalin, and tizanidine was restarted for muscle spasms. She participated in physical therapy, was transitioned to oral pain control, and was discharged home with home health services after an unwitnessed fall with stable repeat imaging.
problems: Displaced intertrochanteric fracture of left femur, initial encounter for closed fracture
Type 1 diabetes mellitus with diabetic polyneuropathy
